sahne: A small campfire at blue hour on a pebbly lakeshore. Dry split logs burn with bright yellow-orange flames and a bed of glowing red embers; a soot-blackened metal kettle hangs over the fire from a simple wooden tripod and a thin plume of steam rises from its spout. The warm firelight spills onto the nearby stones while the evening around it is cool and blue: calm water and a fading twilight sky behind. The fire is clearly the source of heat and light pouring out into the cold evening. No people, no text, no logos.

Close-up on the sideline of a grass football pitch: a young athlete sitting on the grass presses a freshly squeezed instant cold pack against their bare knee with one hand. The cold pack is a plain, completely unprinted white plastic pouch (no text, no logo, no pictograms), slightly puffy, its outer surface beaded with tiny droplets of condensation because it has become very cold. Daylight, shallow depth of field, the rest of the pitch softly blurred behind.

A modern hydrogen fuel-cell city bus standing at a clean, minimalist hydrogen refuelling station at dawn. A thick refuelling hose with a chunky nozzle is plugged into a receptacle on the side of the bus. Under the bus, a few drops of clear water drip from a small exhaust pipe onto the wet asphalt — its only exhaust is water. Soft pink-blue dawn light, a simple white canopy above the dispenser. Absolutely no text, no route numbers, no logos, no signs, no number plates anywhere.

Extreme close-up of a kitchen gas-stove burner ring at night: a crown of clean, steady blue natural-gas flames, each with a crisp, brighter inner cone and faint violet edges, no yellow or orange tips (complete combustion of methane). The dark kitchen behind, a soft reflection of the blue flames on the stainless-steel hob and on the black cast-iron pan support. No text, no logos.

A bright classroom desk with a ball-and-stick molecular model kit laid out on a plain unprinted tray, using standard colours (carbon black, hydrogen white, oxygen red). Clearly visible: a methane model — one black carbon sphere with four white hydrogen spheres arranged tetrahedrally; an oxygen molecule model — two red spheres joined by a double bond made of two curved connectors; a carbon dioxide model — black carbon in the middle and two red oxygens on a straight line, each joined to the carbon by two curved connectors; a water model — one red oxygen with two white hydrogens at a bent angle of about 104 degrees. A teenager's hands are pulling one white hydrogen sphere off the methane model. No text, no labels.

An oxy-acetylene cutting torch slicing through a thick steel plate in a dim workshop: at the nozzle tip a very small, intensely bright blue-white flame cone, and from the cut a dense fan of orange sparks and droplets of molten metal spraying downward. The welder's heavy leather gloves and the edge of a dark protective visor are partly visible at the frame edge. Dark workshop background lit only by the sparks. No text, no logos.

Studio still life on dark slate: a single brilliant-cut colourless diamond sparkling with tiny rainbow flashes sits beside a dull, dark-grey, slightly metallic lump of natural graphite and a snapped wooden pencil whose broken end shows its grey graphite core. The two forms of the same element side by side, soft rim light, shallow depth of field, elegant and minimal. No text, no logos.

A clean school chemistry lab bench: a small glass spirit lamp (alcohol burner) with a cotton wick burns with a calm, mostly pale-blue flame with a faint yellow tip, heating a glass beaker of water that stands on a wire gauze on a metal tripod. A glass thermometer stands in the water showing only plain scale lines (no numbers), and a few tiny bubbles are forming on the inside bottom of the beaker. Soft daylight, uncluttered background. No text, no labels, no logos.

Railway thermite welding at dusk: a ceramic crucible held on a steel frame above the gap between the ends of two steel rails pours a dazzling white-hot stream of molten iron down into a refractory mould clamped around the rail joint. Brilliant sparks, a little white smoke and an intense glow lighting up the gravel ballast and the sleepers; two workers in protective clothing and helmets stand at a safe distance. No text, no logos, no signs.

Macro photograph of a wooden safety match being struck along the striking strip on the side of a plain, completely unprinted matchbox: the match head bursting into flame at the very instant of ignition, a tiny shower of bright sparks and a small curl of smoke, the young flame yellow-orange with a blue base. Pure dark background, crisp detail on the match head. No text, no logos.

A cosy living room fireplace that has NOT been lit: dry split logs and thin kindling sticks neatly stacked in the cold firebox, a crumpled sheet of plain paper underneath, and a closed box of matches resting on the stone hearth. Daylight from a window, everything calm and still: fuel and air together, yet nothing is burning. No fire, no smoke, no text, no logos.

A crash-test laboratory, high-speed photograph: a car's steering-wheel airbag fully inflated a split second after the impact, a crash-test dummy pitching forward into the white cushion, a fine haze of white powder in the air, bright studio lights and a dark background. The dummy and the car interior carry absolutely no text, stickers, numbers, markings or logos.

An effervescent tablet dissolving in a tall, clear drinking glass of water on a bright kitchen table: a dense column of tiny bubbles streams up from the half-dissolved white tablet at the bottom, a thin layer of foam and popping droplets at the surface. Backlit by a window so the bubbles sparkle. No text, no logos, no packaging.

An old bicycle that has been left leaning against a garden wall for years: its chain, chainring, spokes and handlebar covered in orange-brown flaky rust, paint peeling from the frame, weeds and moss around the flat tyres. Soft overcast light, rich texture. No text, no logos, no stickers.

A school chemistry experiment that measures how fast a reaction goes: on a clean lab bench, a conical flask in which a coiled magnesium ribbon fizzes with bubbles in clear acid, closed with a rubber stopper and connected by a short rubber tube to a horizontal glass gas syringe, whose plunger has been pushed partway out by the collected hydrogen gas. Beside it an analogue stopwatch showing only tick marks (no numbers), and a student's hand holding a pencil over a blank notebook. Soft daylight. No text, no numbers, no labels.

Two identical tall glasses side by side on a dark table in a dark room. The left glass is full of hot, steaming water and the glow stick standing in it shines intensely bright green; the right glass is full of ice cubes and cold water and the identical glow stick in it glows only faintly. The glow of the sticks is the main light in the scene. No text, no logos.

A home kitchen at night with the refrigerator door open and its interior light glowing: fresh vegetables, a glass bottle of milk, eggs and covered leftovers neatly stored on the shelves, a cold glass jar beaded with condensation. Calm, clean, inviting. No text, no labels, no logos.

A stainless-steel pressure cooker on a gas stove in a warm home kitchen: its lid locked shut, a strong jet of white steam shooting from the pressure valve on top, the blue gas flame underneath. Warm evening light, a wooden spoon and a few dry beans on the counter beside it. No text, no logos.

The 'elephant toothpaste' demonstration on a school lab bench: a huge, thick column of white foam with a faint yellow tint erupts from a tall clear glass cylinder (no markings) and spills over into a wide plastic tray, a little steam rising from the warm foam. At the side, a teacher's gloved hands and safety goggles resting on the bench. Bright, clean lab. No text, no labels, no logos.

Close-up of several fresh slices of raw potato in a clear glass Petri dish on a kitchen counter. Clear hydrogen peroxide has just been poured over them and a white froth of countless tiny oxygen bubbles is forming on the cut potato surfaces, thickest at the edges. Soft natural light, shallow depth of field. No text, no labels, no bottles with labels.

A cutaway car catalytic converter on a clean workshop table: the stainless-steel shell sliced open lengthwise to reveal the ceramic honeycomb monolith inside, its thousands of tiny square channels coated with a dark grey precious-metal layer. A second loose honeycomb brick lies beside it, seen end-on so the grid of channels is clearly visible. Soft studio light. No text, no logos, no part numbers.

The iodine clock reaction on a bright white lab bench: a row of five identical glass beakers of liquid, each on its own small magnetic stirrer. Three of the beakers have suddenly turned an intense blue-black while two are still perfectly colourless, captured at the very moment of change. Clean, minimal, high-key lighting. No text, no numbers, no labels, no scale markings.

A narrow two-lane mountain road on a sunny late afternoon: a single slow, heavily loaded old truck crawls up the hill and a long line of cars is stuck close behind it, the whole column moving at the truck's pace; no chance to overtake on the winding road. Wide landscape view. No text, no readable number plates, no road signs with text, no logos.

A big city skyline at sunset under a low layer of brownish-orange photochemical smog (nitrogen dioxide haze) lying over the buildings, with heavy traffic on a multi-lane highway in the foreground, headlights and tail lights glowing. The haze is clearly brownish near the ground and clearer higher up. No text, no logos, no signs, no readable number plates.
